questions.question: Parts of speech are classified according to what?
questions.explanation: Parts of speech are basic categories based on function and use in sentences.

questions.question: How many major parts of speech are traditionally recognized?
questions.explanation: Traditionally there are eight major parts of speech.

questions.question: Which part of speech is sometimes added as a ninth in modern grammar?
questions.explanation: Modern grammar sometimes adds determiners as a ninth part.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed among the major parts of speech?
questions.explanation: Tenses are not a part of speech; they are verb forms.

questions.question: Every word in a sentence belongs to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Every word belongs to one of the parts of speech categories.

questions.question: Which of the following is a part of speech?
questions.explanation: Nouns are one of the eight major parts of speech.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists a major part of speech?
questions.explanation: Verbs are one of the major parts of speech.

questions.question: The basic categories into which words are classified are called what?
questions.explanation: Parts of speech are the basic categories for classifying words.

questions.question: A noun is the name of a person, place, animal, thing, idea, or what?
questions.explanation: A noun names a person, place, animal, thing, idea, or quality.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a noun?
questions.explanation: Joy is a noun (abstract).

questions.question: Proper nouns always begin with which type of letter?
questions.explanation: Proper nouns always begin with a capital letter.

questions.question: Which of the following is a proper noun?
questions.explanation: Nigeria is a specific name of a place, so it is a proper noun.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common noun?
questions.explanation: Book is a general name, so it is a common noun.

questions.question: Collective nouns refer to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Collective nouns refer to groups, e.g., class, team.

questions.question: Which of the following is a collective noun?
questions.explanation: Team is a collective noun referring to a group.

questions.question: Tangible nouns refer to things that can be what?
questions.explanation: Tangible nouns refer to physical objects that can be touched.

questions.question: Which of the following is a tangible noun?
questions.explanation: Table is a physical object that can be touched.

questions.question: Abstract nouns refer to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Abstract nouns refer to ideas, qualities, or states, not physical objects.

questions.question: Which of the following is an abstract noun?
questions.explanation: Joy is an abstract noun referring to a feeling.

questions.question: Countable nouns can be what?
questions.explanation: Countable nouns can be counted, e.g., chair, car.

questions.question: Which of the following is a countable noun?
questions.explanation: Car is a countable noun.

questions.question: Uncountable nouns are also known as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Uncountable nouns are often called mass nouns.

questions.question: Which of the following is an uncountable noun?
questions.explanation: Sand is an uncountable noun.

questions.question: Which of the following does a verb express?
questions.explanation: A verb expresses action, event, or state of being.

questions.question: Which of the following is an action verb?
questions.explanation: Write is an action verb showing a physical or mental action.

questions.question: Linking verbs are also called which of the following?
questions.explanation: Linking verbs are also called copula or stative verbs.

questions.question: Which of the following is a linking verb?
questions.explanation: Is is a linking verb showing state.

questions.question: Auxiliary verbs help the main verb to express tense, mood, or what?
questions.explanation: Auxiliary verbs help express tense, mood, or voice.

questions.question: Which of the following is an auxiliary verb?
questions.explanation: Have is an auxiliary verb.

questions.question: A transitive verb takes which of the following?
questions.explanation: Transitive verbs take a direct object.

questions.question: In the sentence She kicked the ball, the verb kicked is what type?
questions.explanation: Kicked takes the direct object the ball, so it is transitive.

questions.question: An intransitive verb has which of the following?
questions.explanation: Intransitive verbs have no object.

questions.question: The verb laughed in She laughed takes which of the following?
questions.explanation: Laughed has no object, so it is intransitive.

questions.question: Which of the following is a modal verb?
questions.explanation: Can is a modal verb.

questions.question: An adjective describes or modifies which of the following?
questions.explanation: Adjectives modify nouns or pronouns.

questions.question: Which of the following is an adjective?
questions.explanation: Happy is an adjective describing a noun.

questions.question: Adjectives give more information about which of the following?
questions.explanation: Adjectives provide more information about nouns or pronouns.

questions.question: The positive degree of an adjective describes without what?
questions.explanation: Positive degree describes without comparison.

questions.question: The comparative degree compares how many things?
questions.explanation: Comparative degree compares two things.

questions.question: Which degree of comparison compares more than two things?
questions.explanation: Superlative degree compares more than two things.

questions.question: What is the comparative form of tall?
questions.explanation: The comparative of tall is taller.

questions.question: What is the superlative form of large?
questions.explanation: Superlative of large is largest.

questions.question: An adverb modifies a verb, an adjective, or which of the following?
questions.explanation: Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.

questions.question: Adverbs show how, when, where, or to what extent an action is done. Which of the following is an adverb?
questions.explanation: Quickly is an adverb showing how an action is done.

questions.question: Which of the following is an adverb of time?
questions.explanation: Today is an adverb of time.

questions.question: The positive degree of an adverb fast is what?
questions.explanation: Positive degree is the base form fast.

questions.question: The comparative degree of fast is what?
questions.explanation: Comparative of fast is faster.

questions.question: The superlative degree of fast is what?
questions.explanation: Superlative of fast is fastest.

questions.question: In the sentence Yesterday, I saw him, the adverb Yesterday is in which position?
questions.explanation: The adverb is at the front position.

questions.question: In the sentence I often visit her, the adverb often is in which position?
questions.explanation: The adverb is in the mid position.
